messages:
michael: Insurance question quick one  my dentist says my plan shows as "inactive" at their office. I logged into the portal and it looks active on my end. What gives?
Rina (People Ops): Hey @michael, this usually happens when carriers provider directory lags or when the office uses an old NPI. Quick steps: get the office name, NPI, and the date/time they tried to verify; well call the carrier and confirm.
Carlos: Happened to me last month; carrier fixed it same day after we submitted the provider's NPI. It was a data sync issue.
Rina (People Ops): Also confirm the plan ID youre presenting (sometimes the practice uses the group number). If the office already collected payment, file a claim/appeal with the itemized receipt; we can help escalate for reimbursement.
michael: Office is "Oakwood Family Dentistry", NPI 1234567890. They called today at 10:04am. They said "inactive" but took a copay anyway.
Rina (People Ops): Thanks. Ill open a ticket with the carrier and attach the provider info + time stamp. Please upload the itemized receipt to the claims portal and reply here with the claim ref if they give one.
Benefits Bot: Carrier ticket opened: TKT-2026-4410. Expect a carrier response in 1-3 business days.
michael: Uploaded receipt. Thanks!
Rina (People Ops): Acked. Well ping once carrier confirms reimbursement. If not resolved in 5 business days we escalate to the carrier resolution team.
